questions.q: Jamia Millia Islamia was founded in 1920 at which place?
questions.explanation: Founded at **Aligarh** in 1920, it moved to Delhi in 1925 and became a central university in 1988.
questions.fact_text: Jamia Millia Islamia was founded in **1920** at **Aligarh** (moved to Delhi in 1925) and became a central university in **1988**. The **Lyngdoh Committee** (2006, chaired by ex-CEC **J.M. Lyngdoh**) framed rules for student union elections.

questions.q: The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) was set up under which law?
questions.explanation: The NHRC is a **statutory** body under the **Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993**; its chair is a former CJI or SC judge.
questions.fact_text: The **NHRC** is a statutory body under the **Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993**; its chairperson is a former Chief Justice of India or former SC judge.

questions.q: Which party rules Tamil Nadu, with C. Joseph Vijay as Chief Minister (2026)?
questions.explanation: Actor-politician **C. Joseph Vijay** heads the **TVK** government in Tamil Nadu.
questions.fact_text: Tamil Nadu is ruled by the **Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK)** with **C. Joseph Vijay** as Chief Minister; DMK chief **M.K. Stalin** condemned the brief detention of MIDS economist **A. Kalaiyarasan**.

questions.q: Dakshin Gangotri, India's first scientific base in Antarctica, was built in:
questions.explanation: **Dakshin Gangotri** was built in **1983-84**, led by geophysicist Harsh Kumar Gupta.
questions.fact_text: **Dakshin Gangotri**, India's first scientific base in Antarctica, was built in **1983-84**, led by geophysicist **Harsh Kumar Gupta**; a documentary, *Miracle in Antarctica*, tells its story.

questions.q: Which is India's research station in the Arctic?
questions.explanation: **Himadri** (2008) is at Svalbard, Norway. Maitri (1989) and Bharati (2012) are in Antarctica. Nodal body: **NCPOR, Goa**.
questions.fact_text: India's Antarctic stations: **Dakshin Gangotri** (1983, now a supply base), **Maitri** (1989) and **Bharati** (2012). India's Arctic station is **Himadri** (2008, Svalbard). Nodal body: **NCPOR**, Goa.

questions.q: The 2024 expert panel on reforming the National Testing Agency (NTA) was headed by:
questions.explanation: Ex-ISRO chief **K. Radhakrishnan** headed the panel. The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024 allows up to 10 years' jail for organised leaks.
questions.fact_text: The 2024 NTA reform panel was headed by ex-ISRO chief **K. Radhakrishnan**. The **Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024** allows up to **10 years** in jail and **₹1 crore** fine for organised paper leaks.

questions.q: Under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006, the minimum marriage age for men is:
questions.explanation: **21** for men and **18** for women.
questions.fact_text: Under the **Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006**, the minimum age is **18 for women and 21 for men**. Child labour below **14** is banned under the Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986 (amended 2016).

questions.q: Under PM Fasal Bima Yojana, the farmer's premium for rabi crops is:
questions.explanation: PMFBY (2016): **2%** kharif, **1.5%** rabi, **5%** commercial/horticultural crops.
questions.fact_text: Rajasthan paid about **₹345 crore** in pending crop insurance claims to farmers in nine districts. **PMFBY** (2016): farmer premium **2%** for kharif, **1.5%** for rabi, **5%** for commercial/horticultural crops.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
1. The Second Judges case (1993) created the collegium system.
2. Under the Third Judges case (1998), the SC collegium is the CJI and the four senior-most judges.
Which is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both are correct. The First Judges case (1981) had given the executive primacy.
questions.fact_text: **Article 124** (SC judges) and **Article 217** (HC judges): appointed by the President after consultation. **First Judges case (1981)**: executive primacy; **Second (1993)**: created the collegium; **Third (1998)**: CJI + 4 senior-most judges for SC, CJI + 2 for HCs. **Memorandum of Procedure**: 1998.

questions.q: The National Judicial Appointments Commission (NJAC), struck down by the SC in 2015, was created by which Amendment?
questions.explanation: The **99th Amendment (2014)** created the NJAC; the SC struck it down in **2015** (Fourth Judges case).
questions.fact_text: The **99th Amendment (2014)** created the **NJAC** (CJI, 2 senior judges, Law Minister, 2 eminent persons); the SC struck it down in **2015** (Fourth Judges case) for violating judicial independence. Abroad: UK's Judicial Appointments Commission has **15** members; South Africa's Judicial Service Commission **23**.

questions.q: Census 2027 door-to-door population enumeration in U.P. and three other poll-bound States starts on:
questions.explanation: It starts **1 Dec 2026** in the four poll-bound States; the rest of India follows in early 2027.
questions.fact_text: Census Phase 2 (population enumeration) door-to-door starts **1 Dec 2026** in U.P. and three other poll-bound States; the rest of India follows in **Feb 2027**. Each enumeration block has 750-800 people; each household takes 20-25 minutes.

questions.q: Besides listing a caste, Census 2027's caste question also offers which two options?
options: 'Does not want to declare' and 'No Caste'
questions.explanation: Caste options include **'does not want to declare'** and **'No Caste'**.
questions.fact_text: New Census questions include caste (for non-SC/ST), religion, parents' place and date of birth, number of bank accounts, spouse's name, nationality, digital literacy, place of COVID-19 vaccination, passport and driving licence, and mobile/Aadhaar/voter ID numbers. Caste options include 'does not want to declare' and 'No Caste'.

questions.q: The 13th ADMM-Plus (ASEAN Defence Ministers' Meeting-Plus) in 2026 was held at:
questions.explanation: Held in **Cebu**; the **Philippines** chairs ASEAN in 2026. Rajnath Singh proposed a defence 'Youth Bridge'.
questions.fact_text: Defence Minister **Rajnath Singh** at the **13th ADMM-Plus** in **Cebu, Philippines** offered India's counter-terrorism expertise, proposed a defence **'Youth Bridge'** with ASEAN, and noted **2026** is the **ASEAN-India Year of Maritime Cooperation**; India and **Malaysia** co-chair the Experts' Working Group on Counter-Terrorism (2024-27).

questions.q: ADMM-Plus brings together the 10 ASEAN members and how many partner countries?
questions.explanation: **8** partners: India, China, Japan, South Korea, Australia, New Zealand, Russia, US. It began in **2010** (Hanoi).
questions.fact_text: **ADMM-Plus** began in **2010** (Hanoi): 10 ASEAN members plus 8 partners (India, China, Japan, South Korea, Australia, New Zealand, Russia, US). The Philippines chairs ASEAN in 2026.

questions.q: The National Food Security Act, 2013 covers up to what share of the urban population?
questions.explanation: Up to **75% rural** and **50% urban**.
questions.fact_text: The **National Food Security Act, 2013** covers up to **75% rural and 50% urban** population; free grain under **PMGKAY** was extended for five years from **1 Jan 2024**.

questions.q: The 24th instalment of PM-KISAN (30 Oct 2026) was released by the PM in which State?
questions.explanation: Released in **Gujarat**: over ₹18,690 crore to 9.34 crore farmers.
questions.fact_text: PM **Narendra Modi** released the **24th instalment** of **PM-KISAN** in Gujarat on 30 Oct: over **₹18,690 crore** to **9.34 crore** farmers.

questions.q: PM-KISAN was launched in February 2019 at:
questions.explanation: Launched at **Gorakhpur**; ₹6,000 a year in three instalments of ₹2,000.
questions.fact_text: **PM-KISAN** (launched Feb 2019 at Gorakhpur) gives **₹6,000 a year** in three instalments of ₹2,000 by direct benefit transfer.

questions.q: The NPPA capped trade margins on 137 non-scheduled anti-cancer medicines at what share of MRP?
questions.explanation: **30% of MRP**, under the Drugs (Prices Control) Order, 2013.
questions.fact_text: The **NPPA** capped trade margins at **30% of MRP** on **137 non-scheduled anti-cancer medicines** under the **Drugs (Prices Control) Order, 2013**, effective **9 Nov**. A 2023 study put average annual out-of-pocket cancer cost at **₹3.31 lakh**.

questions.q: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY was launched on 23 Sept 2018 at:
questions.explanation: Launched at **Ranchi**; ₹5 lakh cover per family per year, run by the National Health Authority.
questions.fact_text: **NPPA** was set up in **1997**. **Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY** (launched 23 Sept 2018, Ranchi) gives cover of **₹5 lakh per family per year**; the National Health Authority runs it.

questions.q: Which Supreme Court judgment recognised transgender persons as a 'third gender'?
questions.explanation: **NALSA (2014)**; Parliament later passed the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019.
questions.fact_text: **NALSA v. Union of India (2014)** recognised transgender persons as a '**third gender**'; Parliament later passed the **Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019**.

questions.q: SEBI got statutory powers in which year?
questions.explanation: Set up in **1988**, statutory under the **SEBI Act, 1992**; HQ Mumbai.
questions.fact_text: **SEBI** was set up in **1988** and got statutory powers under the **SEBI Act, 1992**; HQ **Mumbai**.

questions.q: Who chairs the US Federal Reserve (Oct 2026)?
questions.explanation: Fed Chair **Kevin Warsh**; the Fed held rates at 3.75-4.0%.
questions.fact_text: The **US Federal Reserve** held rates at **3.75-4.0%** (vote 10-2; **Lisa Cook** and **Beth Hammack** wanted a 25 bp hike). Fed Chair **Kevin Warsh** said the FOMC will hold fewer meetings from 2027.

questions.q: The PLI scheme for textiles (approved Sept 2021) has an outlay of:
questions.explanation: **₹10,683 crore**; PLI schemes cover 14 sectors.
questions.fact_text: The PLI scheme for textiles was approved in **Sept 2021** with an outlay of **₹10,683 crore**; PLI schemes cover 14 sectors.

questions.q: Who secured the year-end WTA No. 1 ranking in 2026?
questions.explanation: **Elena Rybakina** (Kazakhstan), who won the US Open.
questions.fact_text: **Elena Rybakina** (Kazakhstan) secured the **year-end WTA No. 1** ranking; she first became No. 1 last month while winning the **US Open**, replacing **Aryna Sabalenka**.

questions.q: Which name does The Hindu now use for the State of Kerala?
questions.explanation: **Keralam**. Renaming a State needs a law of Parliament under **Article 3**.
questions.fact_text: Kerala now goes by **'Keralam'** — the State 'added an m to its name', as *The Hindu* noted; the paper now uses Keralam throughout.

questions.q: 'Kufri Jamunia', a purple potato rich in anthocyanins, was developed by:
questions.explanation: Developed by **ICAR-Central Potato Research Institute, Shimla**.
questions.fact_text: **ICAR-CPRI** developed **Kufri Jamunia**, a purple potato rich in **anthocyanins**: per 100 g, vitamin C 42.75 mg (vs 23.15), zinc 2.28 mg (vs 0.28), iron 3.22 mg (vs 0.57). Notified in Nov 2024; matures in about **90 days**; susceptible to **late blight** (*Phytophthora infestans*).

questions.q: Which is NOT one of CPRI's coloured potato varieties?
questions.explanation: Neelkanth, Manik and Jamunia are coloured varieties; **Kufri Jyoti** is a common white variety.
questions.fact_text: **Central Potato Research Institute (CPRI)** is in **Shimla**; its other coloured varieties are **Kufri Neelkanth** and **Kufri Manik**.

questions.q: In the Niyamgiri case (2013), the Supreme Court let which body decide on Vedanta's bauxite mine?
options: Gram sabhas under the Forest Rights Act, 2006
questions.explanation: The SC left it to the **gram sabhas** under the **FRA, 2006**; all 12 rejected the mine.
questions.fact_text: Niyamgiri (2013): in *Orissa Mining Corporation v. MoEF*, the SC let gram sabhas decide under the **Forest Rights Act, 2006**; all 12 rejected the mine. India has **75 PVTGs**, the most in Odisha.

questions.q: Which Article directs the State to prohibit the slaughter of cows and calves?
questions.explanation: **Article 48** (Directive Principle) covers agriculture and animal husbandry, including cow slaughter.
questions.fact_text: Constitutional link: **Article 48** (Directive Principle) asks the State to organise agriculture and animal husbandry on scientific lines and to prohibit slaughter of cows and calves; cow protection laws are State subjects.

questions.q: Freedom of the press in India flows from:
questions.explanation: Press freedom is part of **freedom of speech and expression, Art. 19(1)(a)**.
questions.fact_text: Press freedom flows from **Article 19(1)(a)**. A 2026 Reuters Institute report says 18-24-year-olds using social media as their main news source rose from **21% (2015) to 39% (2025)**. IT Minister: **Ashwini Vaishnaw**.

questions.q: Which provision of the RTI Act, 2005 did the DPDP Act, 2023 amend on personal information?
questions.explanation: **Section 8(1)(j)** had allowed disclosure of personal information in 'larger public interest'.
questions.fact_text: RTI link: **Section 8(1)(j)** of the RTI Act, 2005 exempted personal information unless 'larger public interest' justified disclosure; the DPDP Act removed that public-interest override.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): A legislature cannot simply declare a court judgment ineffective.
Reason (R): It can validate an act struck down by courts only by removing the defect the courts found.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, R is false
A is false, R is true
questions.explanation: Validation laws must **cure the defect**; overruling a judgment directly breaches the separation of powers.
questions.fact_text: Principle: a legislature can validate an act struck down by courts only by removing the defect the courts found; it cannot simply declare a judgment ineffective (doctrine of separation of powers).
